Spaced repetition, explained

Why reviewing just before you forget beats re-reading

Sam K. · Mar 3, 2026 · 6 min read

Most of what we read is gone within a week. The forgetting curve, first measured by Ebbinghaus, drops steeply in the first day and then flattens out.

Spaced repetition works with that curve instead of against it. You review an idea just as you are about to forget it, and each successful review pushes the next one further out: a day, then three days, then a week, then a month.

Re-reading feels productive because the material looks familiar, but familiarity is not recall. Answering a question from memory is what strengthens the memory.

A simple schedule

  1. Review the next day.
  2. If you remembered, double the gap.
  3. If you forgot, go back to one day.

That is enough to keep most of what you learn for years, for a few minutes a day.
